reviews.summary: Replace the UK-only "The first flat" in the timeline card, and give the reader who wants to order something a delivery-date check.

Our Timeline's countdown shows only when a date is set; "a long partner" isn't idiomatic; "flat" is UK-only. Spanish: "uno que guarda", "ideas para sin motivo" (the site says "porque sí"), the subjectless Letter card, "una tarde de acordarte", and an FAQ question that read as innuendo and strayed from the English.

The keyword is commercial and the top results are things to buy; add a way to order something made specific (star map, print of a place, photo book) with the real date and place on it. All four People also ask questions are answered.

reviews.summary: Both fixes made. It beats the top results because it sorts ideas by how long you've been together and how much time you have, gives lines you can copy and says what to skip, where most lists are undated product roundups.
All eight round-one fixes made correctly. Two Spanish lines still read translated: "Algo que se pide, pero concreto" and "una fiesta de 18 cumpleaños".

The order-something bullet covers the commercial intent. It gives what the ranking roundups of engraved items don't: gifts matched to time together, a time budget, lines to write inside and direct answers to every People also ask question.

reviews.summary: It beats the top results, mostly lists of engravable products, by giving a test for what counts as sentimental, ideas matched to how long you've been together, lines to borrow and a skip list, with the template offered only after the advice.

Both round-two Spanish fixes made correctly; every template claim matches its manifest, schema and Template.tsx, every free-tier line sits inside {note:A|B}, and the Spanish reads as written in Spanish.
All four People also ask questions and the homemade variant's are answered, and the table by time together, lines to write inside and skip list are what none of the ranking product lists offer.
